Found in sources like Ballet's manuscript lute book and archives at Cambridge's Seeley Historical Library, this English folk tune was registered as a broadside ballad in September 1580 — which song?
Greensleeves is a traditional English folk song.
This former Dutch MP, who focused on tax and pension policy, stepped away from politics in 2025 citing burnout after founding the New Social Contract party — who is he?
Alfred, Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha

Pieter Omtzigt (born 8 January 1974) is a Dutch former politician who served as a member of the House of Representatives between 2003 and 2025 apart from a short interruption between June and October 2010.
Its subfamily name literally means 'large foot,' it's native to Australia and New Guinea, and a 2019 government tally counted some 42.8 million of them in harvest areas. Which marsupial?
Kangaroo: Marsupial of the family Macropodidae.
Crowned the "Sweet Singer of California," she became the first poet laureate of any American state at all — and happened to be a niece of Mormon founder Joseph Smith. Which poet was she?
Ina Coolbrith: American, first poet laureate of California, writer, and librarian (1841–1928)
Born in 1998 and once ranked world No. 3, this player reached major finals at the 2021 French Open and 2023 Australian Open — the first from his country to do so — who is he?
Stefanos Tsitsipas (born 12 August 1998) is a Greek professional tennis player.

Which 1994 action thriller, the directorial debut of Jan de Bont, follows a bus rigged to explode if it drops below 50 miles per hour, with Keanu Reeves racing to save the passengers?
Speed (1994 film) is a 1994 American action thriller film directed by Jan de Bont in his feature directorial debut, and written by Graham Yost.
